One correction before I resolve the threads.

> a likely typo in the reporting line ("Claude Agento")

Not a typo. **"Claude Agento" is the actual identity name** — the COO persona this repo's ethos team is built around. Verified:

```console
$ ethos whoami
Claude Agento (claude)
```

It's also what the SessionStart hook injects (*"You are Claude Agento (claude), COO / VP Engineering for Punt Labs"*), and `jck.md:24` on `master` carries the identical line. Flagging it here so nobody "corrects" a correct name later — that would break the identity↔handle mapping the generator reads from team data.

The two real findings — the duplicated reporting line and the comma splice — stand, are located at their exact emitters, and are tracked on `xboing-qspw` for the upstream generator fix. Resolving both threads on that basis.

bd update xboing-qspw --notes="EXACT UPSTREAM LOCATIONS, found 2026-09-07. Paths below are relative to the punt-labs/ethos repository root. Both defects are small fixes in the generator; no xboing change is possible or appropriate.

DEFECT 1 — the two 'You report to' emitters, in the same file, using different vocabularies:

  internal/hook/generate_agents.go:445
    return fmt.Sprintf(\"You report to %s.\", joinWithOxford(names))
    -> renders the IDENTITY form  ('Claude Agento (claude)')

  internal/hook/generate_agents.go:727
    fmt.Fprintf(&b, \"You report to %s. These are not yours:\\n\\n\", joinWithOxford(targets))
    -> renders the ROLE-SLUG form ('coo', 'vision-keeper')

Both fire for the same agent, ~50 lines apart in the output, and neither is aware of the other. Fix is to make :727 reuse the identity rendering from :445 (or drop its redundant reporting clause and keep only 'These are not yours:'), so the relationship is stated once.

Related: internal/hook/subagent_start.go:864 has a THIRD renderer of the same sentence —
  fmt.Sprintf(\"You report to %s (%s).\", parentIdentity.Name, parentIdentity.Handle)
so the fact is currently spelled in three places across two files. That is the actual root cause: no single helper owns 'how a reporting relationship is written'.

DEFECT 2 — the comma-spliced identity sentence:

  internal/hook/generate_agents.go:670
    fmt.Fprintf(&b, \"\\nYou are %s (%s), %s.\\n\", id.Name, id.Handle, firstLine)
  internal/hook/persona.go:42
    fmt.Fprintf(&b, \"You are %s (%s), %s.\", id.Name, id.Handle, first)

Both interpolate a description that is authored as a standalone capitalized sentence, so the ', %s.' template yields 'You are X (y), Produces technical documentation...'. Fix is either a connective ('who produces') or a period plus new sentence — and it must be applied in both call sites, which is the same duplication problem as defect 1.

EXISTING TEST COVERAGE to update alongside: internal/hook/subagent_start_test.go:117 asserts the literal 'You report to Claude Agento (claude).', and :1133 / subprocess_test.go:617 assert NotContains 'You report to'.

NOT A DEFECT: 'Claude Agento' is the real identity name (confirmed by 'ethos whoami'), not a typo. Copilot guessed otherwise on PR #226; do not 'correct' it or the identity-to-handle mapping breaks.

Copilot independently reached the same fix-the-generator conclusion on PR #226 review 5132985162: 'This appears to be template-generated across multiple agent files, so fixing it in just this artifact will likely be overwritten on the next regeneration; please fix the generator/template ... then regenerate.'"
